title: Canonical scalar-extension naturality of affine chart Hom comparisons
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, R a diagram of commutative rings, c an affine limiting cone of its opposite spectrum diagram, i <= j, f:Xi to Spec R(i), U an open cover of the j-base change, and a an affine chart. Let M,N be quasi-coherent modules on U(a). Define the quotient tail J, its monotone representative rep, its starting class t, the chart ring diagram F and the actual starting pullback section modules P,Q as in the explicit constructions in the Lean statement. There exist Hom equivalences alpha at colimit F and beta at each x >= t. For every stage scalar-extension map s, transporting its further scalar extension back by the canonical composition isomorphisms colimitScalarExtensionComp gives a map whose alpha-image satisfies chartOrdinaryMapRecovery with beta(s). There are no arbitrary composition isomorphisms, no independently given limit map phi, no algebraic square hypothesis and no finite-presentation assumption.

source.place: Tag 01ZR first affine proof; Tag 01I6 affine quasi-coherent equivalence; Tags 0095 and 0096 pullback functoriality

proof.text: Apply upperTailChartCone_isLimit. The partial-order quotient is equivalent to the tail, so reindexing preserves the limit. All stages and the vertex are affine by affine base change. Affine spectrum/global sections duality identifies the vertex ring with colimit F. Pullback pasting identifies these charts with the ordinary direct and stage charts. The starting representative is equivalent to j, and thus gives an isomorphic starting chart.

Use the affine quasi-coherent equivalence (Stacks 26.7.5) and its functorial pullback/scalar-extension identification (26.7.3). The actual section modules B(M),B(N) at the starting chart reconstruct M,N. Extend them to the stage and colimit rings. Fully faithfulness gives the two Hom equivalences alpha,beta from these canonical object comparisons.

For each stage map s, tensor associativity and the cocone equation give colimitScalarExtensionComp. Under the affine equivalence, conjugating the further scalar extension by these canonical isomorphisms is ordinary pullback of beta(s). Pullback composition coherence, followed by pullback along the canonical lift from the iterated chart to the direct chart, gives chartOrdinaryMapRecovery. Its lift_snd equation identifies the comparison with the d in that predicate. This only treats the canonical image of s; uniqueness of arbitrary normalized composition isomorphisms and cancellation of the algebraic square are handled in the parent theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_chart_canonical_hom_naturality
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Xi : Scheme.{u}} (f : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j)
    (U : (pullback f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))).OpenCover.{u})
    (a : U.I₀) (ha : IsAffine (U.X a))
    (M N : (U.X a).Modules)
    (hMq : M.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hNq : N.IsQuasicoherent)
    :
    let rep := (OrderEmbedding.ofAntisymmetrization
      (α := {k : I // j ≤ k})).monotone.functor
    let g := U.f a ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))
    let F := rep ⋙ (upperTailChartDiagram R j g).rightOp ⋙ Scheme.Γ
    let t := toAntisymmetrization (· ≤ ·) (⟨j, le_rfl⟩ : {k : I // j ≤ k})
    let B : (U.X a).Modules → ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj t) := fun L ↦ by
      let k := rep.obj t
      let r := Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE k.property))
      change ModuleCat.{u} Γ(pullback r g, ⊤)
      exact ModuleCat.of _ Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd r g)).obj L, ⊤)
    let P := B M
    let Q := B N
    let r₀ := (colimit.ι F t).hom
    let q₀ := baseChangeMap f
      (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
      (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
      (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))
    ∃ α : ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r₀).obj P ⟶
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars r₀).obj Q) ≃
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom q₀ a)).obj M ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom q₀ a)).obj N),
      ∀ (x : Antisymmetrization {k : I // j ≤ k} (· ≤ ·)) (htx : t ≤ x),
        let k := (rep.obj x).val
        let hjk := (rep.obj x).property
        let q := baseChangeMap f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE (hij.trans hjk)))))
          (Over.homMk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hjk)))
            (by dsimp; rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← R.map_comp]; rfl))
        let p := baseChangeMap f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE (hij.trans hjk)))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op k)) (c.w (homOfLE (hij.trans hjk)).op))
        let q₀ := baseChangeMap f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
          (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))
        let w : p ≫ q = q₀ := by
          rw [← baseChangeMap_comp]
          congr 1
          ext
          simpa using c.w (homOfLE hjk).op
        let r := (F.map (homOfLE htx)).hom
        let r₁ := (colimit.ι F x).hom
        ∃ β : ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r).obj P ⟶
            (ModuleCat.extendScalars r).obj Q) ≃
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom q a)).obj M ⟶
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom q a)).obj N),
          ∀ (s : (ModuleCat.extendScalars r).obj P ⟶
              (ModuleCat.extendScalars r).obj Q),
            chartOrdinaryMapRecovery q p q₀ w U a M N
              (α ((colimitScalarExtensionComp F (homOfLE htx) P).hom ≫
                (ModuleCat.extendScalars r₁).map s ≫
                (colimitScalarExtensionComp F (homOfLE htx) Q).inv)) (β s)
